subject.title: fix(models): add provider request rate limits

question: Should OpenClaw core accept this new opt-in model-provider `request.rateLimit` config as the first provider-dispatch slice of outbound API governance?
rationale: The code path is plausible and proven for local dispatch pacing, but it creates a public config contract and intentionally leaves broader budget/status/tool/channel behavior to later work; automation cannot choose that product boundary safely.

options.title: Accept Provider Dispatch First
options.body: Approve the narrow `request.rateLimit` surface after a clean rebase preserves current main's provider egress security boundary.

options.title: Require Broader Limits Design
options.body: Pause this PR until maintainers design the full outbound limits, budgets, status, persistence, and non-provider scope together.

options.title: Close Until Sponsored
options.body: Close this contributor PR as unconfirmed product direction and ask for a maintainer-sponsored design before implementation resumes.

recommendation.title: Accept Provider Dispatch First
recommendation.body: Approve the narrow `request.rateLimit` surface after a clean rebase preserves current main's provider egress security boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the strongest product-scoping signal on the canonical tracker and authored the current-main provider egress change that the PR must reconcile.
